root_causes.description: Telemetry is entirely absent across the call graph (all request/error rates flat at 0), and product-catalog is the heavily-depended-on leaf (frontend, checkout, recommendation all call it), so its stall/failure best explains a total telemetry blackout. No CPU, restart, log, or event corroboration exists, so confidence is low.

evidence.expected_baseline: request_rate > 0 req/s under continuous load-generator traffic

root_causes.description: A crashed/unavailable product-catalog pod would explain loss of all request telemetry from the dependency-heavy leaf, but zero restart counts and no K8s events contradict a crash.

evidence.expected_baseline: 0 under healthy operation; increase expected on crash

root_causes.description: Frontend, the entry point for all load-generator traffic, also reports zero request and error telemetry, consistent with a telemetry-pipeline (OTel collector) outage rather than a single service fault; classified unknown due to absence of any span/log/event signal.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend error_rate < 0.01 with non-zero request_rate under load
frontend serves all ingress traffic; should be > 0
continuous application log stream from otel-demo services

remediation_steps: Verify the OTel Collector / telemetry pipeline is running and scraping; check collector pod health and exporter connectivity for otel-demo.
Confirm product-catalog pod status: kubectl get pods -n otel-demo -l app.kubernetes.io/name=product-catalog and kubectl top pod to compare CPU against requests/limits.
If a cpu_stress/dependency fault is injected against product-catalog, stop the chaos/flagd fault injection to relieve starvation.
Restart product-catalog and any stalled upstream (frontend, checkout, recommendation) if readiness probes have failed, then confirm request/error telemetry resumes.
Re-check request_rate and error_rate for product-catalog and frontend to confirm telemetry restoration.
